preserving.description: Builds the whole output in memory and writes it once with a single write call.

files.solve.py:
with open("matrix.tsv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    rows = [line.split("\t") for line in fh.read().split("\n") if line != ""]

text = ""
for column in zip(*rows):
    text += "\t".join(column) + "\n"

with open("transposed.tsv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    fh.write(text)

preserving.description: Uses explicit index loops instead of zip to transpose.

files.solve.py:
with open("matrix.tsv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    rows = [line.split("\t") for line in fh.read().split("\n") if line != ""]

height = len(rows)
width = len(rows[0]) if rows else 0
out = []
for j in range(width):
    out.append("\t".join(rows[i][j] for i in range(height)) + "\n")

with open("transposed.tsv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    fh.writelines(out)

preserving.description: Uses pathlib and splitlines-free parsing with bytes-preserving write through write_text.

files.solve.py:
from pathlib import Path

raw = Path("matrix.tsv").read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
rows = [line.split("\t") for line in raw.split("\n") if line]
transposed = [list(col) for col in zip(*rows)]
lines = ["\t".join(col) + "\n" for col in transposed]
Path("transposed.tsv").write_bytes("".join(lines).encode("utf-8"))
